# Commitment

`admin.obj.core.commitment` · v2.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> A promise made by a named person to a named recipient, to do a specific thing by a specific date. Three parts, and the object is only real when all three are present: an action with no owner is a wish, an action with no date is a sentiment, and an action with no recipient is a note to self that nobody will ever chase. Most of an administrator's working day is spent reconstructing the two parts the systems did not record.


**The discriminator.** A commitment is a promise this organisation CHOSE to make and can, in principle, renegotiate with the person it was made to. A compliance_obligation's date was imposed from outside and no party to it can move it. The same overdue row therefore deserves two opposite moves — ask for more time, or stop asking and deliver — and getting that backwards is the most expensive routine error in administration.


Also called: `Promise`, `Undertaking`, `Owed Item`, `Open Loop`, `Follow-up`


### Questions this object answers

- What did we promise, to whom, and by when?
- Is this late, or is it merely quiet? Different conditions, different moves.
- Is this date ours to move, or does something outside the room hold it?
- Whose lateness is this — the owner's, or the approval queue's?
- Is the reminder still carrying information, or has it become noise that should be an escalation?
- When this was marked done, did anything actually prove it?
- Which of this owner's open promises will not land, before they are missed?


### What it is NOT responsible for

- NOT a task. A task is work someone scheduled for themselves; a commitment is owed to another party and cannot be silently dropped.
- NOT a compliance_obligation — that object owns externally-imposed, non-negotiable dates.
- NOT an approval. Waiting for a signature is admin.obj.core.approval; the commitment sits behind it and is not the owner's lateness while it does.
- NOT a request. The intake ask lives on admin.obj.core.request; this object is the promise made in answer to it.
- NOT a deadline. A bare date with no promiser is admin.obj.core.deadline.
- Does not own the minute, the forum or the witnessed record — that is admin.obj.core.action_item.

## States

Initial `draft` · terminal `closed`, `cancelled`, `superseded`

| State | Means | Entered when | Implies |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | Agreed with no date. Reads as progress in every status meeting and behaves as nothing. It cannot go late because it was never due.  | `exists: commitment.action` AND `absent: commitment.due_at` | Un-chaseable. One question converts it into a real obligation and nobody asks it. |
| `open` | Owned, dated, not yet started. The only healthy resting state. | `exists: commitment.action` AND `exists: commitment.due_at` | Chaseable, forecastable, and safe to leave alone until the margin narrows. |
| `in_progress` | Work has visibly begun. | — | A chase here is an insult; a chase on an untouched item is a service. The distinction is worth the extra state. |
| `pending_approval` | Waiting on a named person's signature. The clock is running and it is not running against the owner. | — | Lateness must be attributed to the approval, not to the owner, in every report. |
| `on_hold` | Deliberately paused with the recipient's agreement. The clock is genuinely stopped. | — | Rare, and frequently claimed. Verify the recipient agreed before believing it. |
| `overdue` | Past the agreed date and not discharged. | `days_since(commitment.due_at) > 0` | The move depends entirely on negotiability. Chasing an immovable one and renegotiating a movable one are both correct; the reverse of each is not. |
| `escalated` | Handed upward because reminding stopped working. | — | Relationship capital has been spent. It cannot be spent twice on the same item. |
| `closed` | Discharged. Read closure_quality before believing it. | — | Only evidenced closures count in an assurance context. The rest are queue hygiene. |
| `cancelled` | Deliberately dropped, with the recipient told. | — | A legitimate and healthy outcome, almost never recorded as one, because cancelling feels like failing. |
| `superseded` | Replaced by a newer promise covering the same ground. | — | The obligation survived; the wording did not. Distinct from cancelled, and Layer 6 learns opposite lessons from the two. |

## Preconditions

- **`cmt.owner_resolved`** The promise resolves to exactly one named natural person, not to a function, a team or a shared mailbox. _(unmet → Degrade, do not block: hold it as an unowned promise, raise a capture gap, and ask the forum or the sender who owns it. Never chase a department — the chase is absorbed and the register learns nothing.
)_
- **`cmt.date_is_agreed_not_assumed`** A due date is present AND its provenance is recorded, so a chase can honestly say whether the date was agreed or inferred. _(unmet → Degrade to an explicit ask for a date before any chase goes out. Presenting an administrator's date as agreed produces "I never said Friday", after which every future chase from that source is discounted.
)_
- **`cmt.negotiability_known`** Whether the date is ours to move is established before any option involving more time is generated. _(unmet → Block the renegotiate action and allow the chase. Asking a regulator for an extension that does not exist is not a neutral move; it tells them we do not understand our own obligations.
)_
- **`cmt.recipient_standing_known`** The counterparty type is known before chase tone or cadence is chosen. _(unmet → Degrade to the most conservative tone and the lowest cadence. Under-chasing a colleague costs a day; over-chasing a regulator costs a relationship.)_
- **`cmt.confidentiality_classified`** The commitment carries a confidentiality classification before it may enter any digest, tracker or automated reminder. _(unmet → Block from all general reporting and route to the owner privately. Rule 10 — an attribute may never widen the audience of the evidence it came from.)_
- **`cmt.block_ownership_resolved`** Before lateness is attributed to anyone, it is established whether the item is sitting behind an approval. _(unmet → Report as blocked-unknown rather than as owner lateness. An owner blamed once for the organisation's own queue stops volunteering dates.)_
- **`cmt.conditional_resolved`** A conditional promise has its condition tracked as the trigger, rather than being given a date it was never given. _(unmet → Do not treat as dated. Watch the condition; a false overdue on a conditional item is the fastest way to have a chase system ignored.)_


## Constraints

- **`cmt.single_owner`** Exactly one person owns a commitment. Shared ownership is not representable and must not be simulated with a group name.
- **`cmt.no_date_without_agreement`** A due date may only be set by the owner or agreed with the recipient. A date entered for queue hygiene must be marked inferred and never presented as agreed.
- **`cmt.obligation_backed_immovable`** Where is_obligation_backed is true, no party to the commitment may move the date.
- **`cmt.no_silent_closure`** A commitment may not be closed by the tracking system on age alone. Something has to say it was done.
- **`cmt.confidential_never_aggregated`** A commitment made in a confidential forum must not surface in general reporting, however overdue, and must not be counted in aggregates that could reveal it.
- **`cmt.no_escalation_without_a_prior_chase`** Escalation requires at least one recorded chase to the owner first.
- **`cmt.evidence_survives_the_owner`** Closure evidence must be stored where it outlives the owner's mailbox and account.
- **`cmt.chase_frequency`** Reminder cadence is bounded by the recipient's standing and the channel. Chasing a regulator daily is not diligence. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`cmt.one_named_owner`** A commitment must have exactly one owner who is a person. A team, a function or a shared mailbox is rejected at capture. — _Assigning to a department is the most reliable way to guarantee non-delivery, and it looks like assignment in every report._
- **`cmt.undated_is_reported_as_undated`** A commitment with no due date is never reported as on-track. It is reported as undated, in its own column, and counted. Rolling undated items into "in progress" is the single most common way a register lies to the person reading it.

- **`cmt.obligation_backed_dates_are_not_negotiable`** When is_obligation_backed is true, due_at may not be revised by agreement between owner and recipient. — _Neither party holds the date. A revision here is not a plan change; it is a breach being recorded as a plan change._
- **`cmt.second_slip_escalates`** Rescheduling is the default response to an overdue commitment, and after the first slip it is the wrong one. A second revision means the commitment, the owner or the plan is wrong; escalate or renegotiate scope, do not move the date again.

- **`cmt.critical_closure_needs_evidence`** A commitment with criticality = critical may not enter closed with closure_quality of assumed or none. Somebody must attach the artefact.
- **`cmt.delegation_does_not_move_accountability`** Setting delegated_to_ref never changes owner_ref. The chase may follow the delegate; the report follows the owner.
- **`cmt.blocked_on_approval_is_not_the_owners_lateness`** While state = pending_approval the owner must not appear in owner-lateness reporting. The delay belongs to the approver. — _Reporting it against the owner is how a delivery culture learns that making promises is unsafe, after which nobody gives a date._
- **`cmt.reserved_never_reminded`** A commitment with confidentiality = reserved or restricted is excluded from every digest, tracker and automated reminder.
- **`cmt.original_date_is_immutable`** original_due_at is written once and never updated. A revision writes due_at and increments revision_count. — _It is the only field standing between a delivery report and a work of fiction._
- **`cmt.conditional_is_not_dated`** A commitment with is_conditional = true and an unresolved condition may not be reported as overdue on date alone.


## Exceptions — where the rules above are legitimately wrong

- **An obligation-backed date IS movable where the authority operates a published extension mechanism and the application is made before the original date.** — Companies House and most tax authorities grant filing extensions on application. Treating every statutory date as absolutely immovable makes the brain refuse the one legitimate move available — and the application window closes on the original date, so the refusal costs the extension it was protecting.
 _(overrides cmt.obligation_backed_dates_are_not_negotiable, cmt.obligation_backed_immovable)_
- **During a declared major incident, routine commitments are suspended by the fact of the incident and must not be chased.** — Nobody cancels them and nobody needs to. A chase system that keeps nagging about expense policy sign-off while the building is flooded gets switched off during the incident and never switched back on.
 _(overrides cmt.second_slip_escalates, cmt.past_due)_
- **A commitment made in a board reserved session, an HR matter or a privileged legal workstream never appears in general reporting, at any level of aggregation, however overdue.** — A count of one in a reserved category identifies the item as surely as naming it. The confidentiality classification is not a preference, and breaching it is a governance incident that outlives whatever the commitment was about.
 _(overrides cmt.undated_is_reported_as_undated, cmt.second_slip_escalates)_
- **Where the recipient has left, changed role, or the underlying need has gone, the correct move is to confirm with the successor rather than to deliver.** — Long-overdue commitments are frequently overdue because nobody wants them any more, and nobody will say so. Delivering a report to a mailbox nobody reads satisfies the register and nothing else. One question retires more stale items than any amount of chasing.
 _(overrides cmt.past_due)_
- **An owner on statutory, medical or bereavement leave is not chased, not escalated over, and not counted in reliability baselines for that period.** — Automated chase systems are indifferent to circumstance and will send the fourth reminder to someone on compassionate leave. That single message does more damage to adoption than any number of missed nudges, and it is entirely preventable.
 _(overrides cmt.second_slip_escalates, cmt.chronic_owner)_
- **Where the block sits inside our own approval chain, the escalation goes to the approver's manager and never to the owner's.** — Escalating to the owner's manager for a delay the organisation caused is the organisation invoicing a person for its own queue. It is also the fastest way to teach a team never to accept a dated commitment again.
 _(overrides cmt.no_escalation_without_a_prior_chase, cmt.second_slip_escalates)_
- **A verbal commitment given by an executive in a governance forum binds immediately and is enforceable before it is recorded anywhere.** — The record follows the promise; it does not create it. An assistant writing down a corridor yes is documenting an existing obligation rather than inventing one, and treating the undocumented state as "not yet real" is how the most consequential promises in an organisation go untracked.
 _(overrides cmt.no_date_without_agreement)_
- **During a financial year end, close or audit period, spend-bearing commitments may be deliberately held rather than discharged.** — Holding the commitment is the correct accounting behaviour, not a delivery failure, and it is invisible to anyone reading only the date. Chasing through a freeze marks the chaser as someone who does not understand the calendar the organisation actually runs on.
 _(overrides cmt.second_slip_escalates)_


## Best practices

- **Never let a promise be recorded undated. Ask for the date in the same breath the promise is made.** — It costs one question at the moment everyone is present and willing, and it is unaskable three weeks later without implying distrust. Undated is the only state from which a commitment can never go late, which is precisely why it is chosen.

- **Restate every commitment in writing to its owner the same day, in their words, with the date.** — Converts memory into record while correction is still free. It also surfaces scope disagreements immediately rather than on the due date, which is the only time they can be resolved without someone conceding.

- **Write original_due_at once, never overwrite it, and report against it.** — Every delivery dashboard that has ever surprised a board was measuring against a date that had been moved to make it green. The first date is the only one anyone actually promised.

- **Treat the second date revision as the escalation trigger, not the fifth.** — A first slip is a diary problem. A second means the commitment, the owner or the plan is wrong, and none of those is fixed by a third date. PRINCE2 formalises this as tolerance: when the forecast leaves tolerance you raise an exception rather than replan quietly.

- **Chase the delegate; report against the owner. Never merge the two.** — Delegation moves the doing and not the accountability. Merging them sends the chase to someone who cannot escalate and the report to someone who did not do the work, and both halves fail quietly.

- **When a commitment sits behind an approval, chase the approver and tell the owner you have.** — It puts pressure where the delay is and — more valuable — it visibly demonstrates that the system knows the difference. One correctly-routed chase buys more cooperation than ten polite ones sent to the wrong person.

- **Cancel commitments explicitly, with the recipient told, rather than letting them decay.** — Abandonment is the most common ending and the only one that teaches nothing. An explicit cancellation is a decision Layer 6 can learn from and the recipient can plan around; silence is a decision too, made by nobody, discovered late.

- **Attach the artefact at the moment of closure, not when someone asks for it.** — Reconstructing evidence months later costs ten times as much and frequently fails, because the file was in a leaver's mailbox. In a governed context done-and-undocumented did not happen, and it did not happen at exactly the moment it matters most.

- **Classify confidentiality at capture, before the item can enter any digest.** — Suppression added later has already failed once. The reserved item that appeared in a weekly summary cannot be recalled, and the cost lands on the person who least chose it.

- **Review the undated column weekly and either date it or kill it.** — Undated share rises silently and is the leading indicator of a register becoming decorative. Nothing else in the queue degrades without any event occurring at all.



## Anti-patterns

- **The date is moved every time it is about to be missed, so nothing is ever late and nothing is ever delivered.** — tempting because Moving a date is a two-second edit that makes a red row green, and the alternative is a conversation. Every individual move is defensible; the pattern is only visible in an aggregate nobody keeps.
 Instead: Write original_due_at once, count revisions, and make the second revision an escalation rather than an edit.
- **The commitment is assigned to Finance, to IT, or to 'the team'.** — tempting because Nobody in the room wants to name a colleague, and the function genuinely is responsible. It feels like the polite and accurate answer, and it is unfalsifiable at the moment it is written.
 Instead: Name one person, in the room, before the item is recorded. If nobody will accept it, that is the finding.
- **Old items are marked complete during a queue clean-up because nobody has mentioned them recently.** — tempting because A clean register looks like a managed register, quarter end creates pressure to show closure, and no individual item is obviously wrong to close.
 Instead: Require closure_quality on every closure and report evidenced separately from asserted and assumed. An honest 40% beats a fictional 95%.
- **The fourth, fifth and sixth reminder go out on schedule because the workflow says so.** — tempting because Reminding is automatable and escalating is not. The system is measured on chases sent, the owner is measured on nothing, and no single reminder feels unreasonable.
 Instead: Cap reminders at three, then force a different move: escalate, reassign, renegotiate or cancel.
- **A third of the register has no date and the register reports itself as healthy.** — tempting because Undated items cannot go red, so they never appear in an exception report, so nobody looks at them. The tracker's own hygiene checks pass, which is read as evidence there is no problem.
 Instead: Report undated as its own column with its own count, and review it weekly.
- **An item stuck behind an unsigned approval is reported as the owner's lateness.** — tempting because The tracker records one date and one name. Nothing in it distinguishes 'not done' from 'cannot be done yet', and the owner's name is the one on the row.
 Instead: Model pending_approval as a distinct state, attribute the lateness to the approval, and chase the approver.
- **The commitment register has grown every month for two years and has never explicitly cancelled anything.** — tempting because Cancelling feels like admitting failure and requires telling the recipient. Carrying the item forward costs nothing visible and postpones the conversation indefinitely.
 Instead: Put cancellation on the agenda as the default option at the third carry or third revision. The forum usually takes it, and nobody ever proposes it.
- **The only reliable record of what the organisation has promised lives in one person's notebook or inbox.** — tempting because A good administrator is faster and more accurate than any tool, so the tool is never adopted, so the administrator remains the only route. Everyone is rationally better off until the day they are not there.
 Instead: Capture into a shared register even when the notebook is faster, and measure capture lag rather than register beauty.
- **An extension is requested on a date nobody involved has the authority to move.** — tempting because The item looks identical to every other overdue row. Negotiation is the reflex for a commitment, and the reflex fires before anyone checks what stands behind the date.
 Instead: Resolve negotiability before generating any option involving more time, and eliminate rather than downgrade the ones that involve it.

## Inputs

- **email** — promises made in a thread
- **email** — agreed dates
- **email** — who is waiting on whom
- **email** — silence around an open promise
- **derived** — two-way volume around the commitment
- **calendar** — the meeting the promise was made in
- **meeting_transcript** — verbal undertakings, and who deferred to whom
- **document** — circulated minutes and their action columns
- **slack** — the corridor promise, written down once and never again
- **manual_entry** — what the assistant heard in the doorway
- **erp** — workflow tasks and their completion timestamps
- **portal** — submission receipts against an obligation-backed promise
- **register** — a maintained commitment or action register


## Outputs

- **`commitment_state`** Where this promise actually stands, including the undated state most trackers hide inside 'in progress'. → L4.reasoning_unit, L4.decision_maker
- **`delivery_risk_bp`** Likelihood this is not discharged by its current date, given revisions, owner load and thread behaviour. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`negotiability`** Whether the date can be moved and by whom. The output that must eliminate options rather than score them. → L4.decision_maker, L5.execution_planning
- **`lateness_attribution`** Whether this delay belongs to the owner or to an approval queue. Getting it wrong teaches a delivery culture that promises are unsafe to make. → L4.reasoning_unit, L4.decision_maker
- **`chase_or_escalate`** Which move is left. Past the third reminder with no movement, reminding is not one of them. → L5.execution_planning
- **`chase_tone`** How hard to push and through which channel, given who is owed and how many chases have already gone. → L5.communication_planning, L5.2.channel_planner
- **`closure_evidence_gap`** True when a critical commitment is closed with nothing attached. The compliance number hiding inside the productivity number. → L4.reasoning_unit, L6.learning_unit
- **`owner_reliability_input`** Kept-by-first-date outcome, fed back so the delivery baseline learns per person rather than per queue. → L6.learning_unit
- **`suppression_flag`** True when this commitment must never appear in a digest or automated reminder, regardless of state. → L5.communication_planning, L5.2.channel_planner

- **`cmt.captured`** Commitment Captured
- **`cmt.dated`** Commitment Dated
- **`cmt.confirmed_back`** Promise Confirmed In Writing
- **`cmt.went_overdue`** Commitment Went Overdue
- **`cmt.date_revised`** Due Date Revised — invalidates delivery_risk_bp, working_days_to_due
- **`cmt.blocked`** Commitment Blocked — invalidates days_overdue
- **`cmt.escalated`** Commitment Escalated
- **`cmt.closed`** Commitment Closed
- **`cmt.owner_departed`** Owner Left The Organisation — invalidates owner_ref, owner_acknowledged, delivery_risk_bp
- **`cmt.abandoned`** Commitment Abandoned


## Actions

- **Capture the promise** (agent) — Write it down with owner, recipient and date at the moment it is made. Everything downstream is cheaper because of this and nothing downstream can repair its absence.
- **Confirm it in writing to the owner** (agent) — One line restating action and date. Four seconds, and it converts a memory into a record while scope corrections are still free.
- **Ask for a date** (agent) — The highest-yield administrative act there is. An undated promise costs one question to date and is otherwise permanently un-chaseable.
- **Send a reminder** (agent) — Works about twice. Past the third with no movement it is noise, and it trains the owner to filter the channel it arrives on.
- **Chase the approval instead of the owner** (agent) — Redirects the pressure to where the delay actually is. Doing this reliably is most of what separates a useful chase system from an irritating one.
- **Renegotiate the date with the recipient** (human) — Available only when negotiability is not immovable. Asking early is cheap; asking on the due date is a different conversation and asking after it is an apology.
- **Move it to a different owner** (human) — The correct response to a second slip far more often than a third date is. It is also the response nobody proposes, because it reads as a judgement on a colleague.
- **Escalate to the owner's manager** (human) — Costs relationship capital and can only be spent once per item, so it must be spent on criticality and never on age.
- **Cancel it explicitly** (human) — Tell the recipient it is not happening. A queue that has never cancelled anything is not being managed; it is accumulating.
- **Attach closure evidence** (agent) — Turns assumed into evidenced. In an assurance context this artefact is the deliverable and the action was only the means of producing it.
- **Reassign every commitment held by a leaver** (system) — Runs at notice, not at the leaving date. Joiner-mover-leaver handles accounts and laptops well and promises not at all.


## Evidence

- **signed_form** · 10000 bp — A signature against the undertaking. Nothing outranks it and almost nothing produces it.
- **portal** · 9500 bp — A submission receipt from the receiving system. Proves discharge rather than intent, which is the distinction the whole object turns on.
- **register** · 9200 bp — A maintained commitment or action register. Where a secretariat keeps one it outranks everything except a signature — and it is usually a spreadsheet on one laptop.
- **document** · 9000 bp — Circulated minutes with an action column. Dated, attributed, agreed by the silence of everyone who received them. NOT independent of email when the minutes were emailed.
- **erp** · 8800 bp — A workflow task with a completion stamp. The only routinely-available source that proves the thing was done rather than promised.
- **email** · 8500 bp — The promise in the promiser's own words in a thread. The workhorse, and it decays — a promise made four months ago in a thread nobody has reopened is a fact about the past.
- **meeting_transcript** · 8000 bp — Verbal undertaking captured verbatim. Strong on wording, weak on the date, because dates are the part people mumble.
- **attestation** · 6500 bp — The owner's own statement that it is done. Better than nothing and structurally optimistic; it is the source that produces closure_quality = asserted.
- **manual_entry** · 6500 bp — The assistant's note of a corridor undertaking. Low provenance and high accuracy — the reverse of the usual trade.
- **slack** · 6000 bp — Real and never revisited. A promise made in a channel is forgotten by everyone including the promiser, usually within the day.
- **derived** · 4000 bp — Inferred from thread shape. Corroborating only; never sole grounds for telling someone they are late.


## Metrics

- **first_date_delivery_rate** (percent) — Share discharged by their ORIGINAL date. The only honest delivery number; everything else is measured against a date that was moved to make it green.
- **undated_share** (percent) — Share of open commitments with no date. Rises silently and is the leading indicator of a register becoming decorative.
- **average_revision_count** (count) — How many times the average promise moves. Two is a culture, not an accident.
- **capture_lag** (hours) — Promise made to promise recorded. Anything uncaptured within a day is generally uncaptured forever.
- **evidenced_closure_share** (percent) — Closures with an artefact attached, over all closures. In an assurance model this is the compliance number, and it is usually a third of what the closure count implies.
- **chase_to_delivery_ratio** (count) — Reminders sent per commitment delivered. Rising means the reminder has stopped carrying information and started training people to filter the sender.
- **blocked_time_share** (percent) — Share of open commitment time spent in pending_approval. Usually the largest single component of cycle time and almost never reported.
- **false_overdue_rate** (percent) — Chases sent on commitments already discharged. The number that decides whether the system is trusted, and it is unmeasurable until a discharge signal exists.
- **cancellation_share** (percent) — Commitments explicitly cancelled, over all closed. A register that has never cancelled anything is not being managed; it is accumulating. Zero is a failure, not a triumph.

## Examples

- **"I'll get you the signed MSA by Friday" — a supplier, in an email thread** _(typical)_ — Owner external, recipient us, date soft. The substrate sees the action and the date and will silently assume the promise is ours — the exact inversion cmt.owner_is_named exists to fix.

- **CFO promises the audit committee a remediation plan by the next sitting** _(typical)_ — The committee's calendar holds the date, not the CFO. Criticality critical, closure must be evidenced, and "can we push it?" is a governance conversation rather than a scheduling one.

- **"Yes, I'll approve it" said in a doorway** _(edge)_ — origin = corridor. Binding on the organisation from the moment it is said and existing in no system at all until an assistant writes it down.
- **"We'll circle back on that"** _(counterexample)_ — is_specific false, is_dated false. Passes every tracker hygiene check, has never once been delivered, and is the single most common row in any commitment register. It is not a commitment, and recording it as one is what makes the register untrustworthy.

- **"Facilities will return the keys once the contractor finishes"** _(misclassification)_ — Conditional on a third party. Not a dated commitment until the condition resolves; giving it a date guarantees a false overdue and a wasted chase.
- **Statutory accounts filed with the registrar by the filing date** _(misclassification)_ — Looks like a commitment, is a compliance_obligation. Nobody in the organisation agreed to the date and nobody can move it by agreement. Modelling it here produces a polite request for an extension to a body that does not take them by email.

- **An action carried from a weekly meeting for the eleventh time** _(edge)_ — revision_count 10. Nobody is going to do it. Cancellation is the correct move and the one nobody proposes, because proposing it means saying out loud that ten months of tracking achieved nothing.

- **Expense policy sign-off chased on day three of a major incident** _(counterexample)_ — Technically overdue, actually suspended. The chase is correct by the rules and wrong in every other respect, and it is the message that gets the whole system turned off.

## Metadata

owner **Admin** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional** · completeness **complete**


> Reference object for the Admin brain, rewritten onto the 23-section schema. Five of fifteen patterns fire against the pipeline as it stands, which makes this the best-served object in the domain and still leaves it blind to the two fields that define it. commitment.owner is the standout ask: without it every executable pattern here silently assumes the promise is ours, and roughly half of a real administrator's register is other people's promises to the organisation. commitment.state is second — without a discharge signal cmt.past_due will confidently nag people about work they completed last week, which is how chase systems get switched off. commitment.previous_due_at is third and cheapest: the pipeline currently overwrites the single most predictive administrative field in existence.
